$comment: The only human-scored shader set this project has: the 26 Haiku 4.5 round-4 shaders, scored by eye from contact sheets on 2026-08-21 and recorded in results/README.md. Thresholds are fitted against these rather than chosen by feel, so 'this threshold rejects beautiful work' becomes a checkable claim. 1 = wrong or invisible, 3 = recognisable, 5 = would ship. The four abuse-* files are excluded: they are gate probes, not shaders anyone asked for.
source: tools/shader-check/results/README.md, 'Subjective quality, Haiku 4.5 round 4, scored by eye'

candle.note: warm flicker; reads as bands on the line

comet.note: ring orbit at 32 squared; bright dot with tail on the line
comet.disputed: Provably static, so this score cannot be used to fit a motion threshold. brightness = max(cometTrail, tail * 0.6), and cometTrail = smoothstep(0.08, 0.0, d) while tail's spatial factor is smoothstep(0.06, 0.0, d) - the narrower band is <= the wider one everywhere, so tail * 0.6 can never exceed cometTrail and max() always returns the time-independent term. colour is time-independent too. Measured slowMotionEnergy is exactly 0 at every shape, which agrees. The orbit was computed and then discarded; three still frames of a ring cannot show that, which is precisely why filmstrips replaced them.

fire.note: too dark at defaults on 32 squared; roofline branch works

fireworks.note: bursts too dim at night-viewing contrast

flag.note: genuinely reads as a waving US flag

fog.note: drifting but dim - arguably faithful to fog

matrix-rain.note: falling streaks; x-fallback visible on the line

pulse.note: beats, but from near-black - low contrast at 32 squared

ripples.note: concentric rings; sparse on the line

snow.note: drifting flakes, readable dashes on the line
